title: Causal drivers of Alzheimer's disease beyond amyloid
bottleneck: Decades of amyloid-focused research produced drugs that clear plaques without meaningful cognitive benefit: a 2026 Cochrane review of 17 trials and 20,342 patients found anti-amyloid drugs had little to no impact on decline. The field still lacks a validated causal model integrating tau, neuroinflammation, vascular, metabolic, and microbial contributors.
why_it_blocks: Alzheimer's is the most expensive and feared disease of aging; continuing to pour the majority of funding into a hypothesis that has failed clinically delays real disease-modifying therapies by decades.
current_state: Lecanemab and donanemab are approved but offer marginal slowing with brain swelling and bleeding risks; the UK and France declined coverage. Research is pivoting toward tau, microglial, and metabolic targets, but no replacement causal framework commands consensus.
